absent: Field layouts and sizes of run queue, task, task group, load weight, housekeeping state, NUMA mask tables, and clamp request and aggregate objects.
Numeric values of capacity scale, idle weight, priority tables, clamp indexes, housekeeping types, run queue flag bits, and task state and queueing markers.
Update paths and lifetime rules for housekeeping masks, NUMA masks and levels, load tables, and clamp defaults beyond what the fragments show.
Callers, ordering, and cross-processor effects of tick permission queries, tickless kicks, idle balance soft processing, and reschedule notifications.
Semantics of fair bandwidth objects, hierarchical quota accounting, extended scheduler dispatch, bypass, rescue, and per-queue stop indication.
Traversal reentrancy, reference stability, and error propagation expectations for group hierarchy visitors and control group task iteration.
Wait-channel computation, state matching prerequisites, and deactivation and migration interactions with sleep and wake paths.
System state values, boot sequencing for secondary processors, and sysctl parsing and permission behavior for clamp controls.

findings.text: Provides the processor set designated for a housekeeping type, falling back to the full possible set when no override is active or the type is not isolated.

Checked dereference of a per-type housekeeping mask is authorized during very early boot for domain isolation, and thereafter by hotplug write protection or cpuset protection; other domain contexts fail validation while non-domain types are always authorized.
Representative selection for an isolated type remains on the caller when overrides are inactive or the type is unflagged, and otherwise seeks an online member of that type with locality preference.
Representative selection emits a one-time warning when a flagged type has no online member outside the expected early boot timer case while the system is running.

Closest-member lookup is build dependent: one build always reports absence, while the NUMA aware build intersects the requested set with successive locality masks under read side protection and reports the earliest hit.
NUMA aware closest-member lookup holds read side protection while consulting the shared NUMA mask table and level count.
Reports whether the run queue bound to a processor is currently hosting only its idle thread.
Idle wake for a remote processor marks its idle thread for rescheduling and notifies it unless the target is in a polling phase; a request targeting the caller has no effect.
Full tickless wake treats offline targets as already satisfied and requests a tick re-evaluation kick for tickless-full members, including the caller when its tick is stopped.
Unified tickless wake entry prefers the full tickless kick path and falls back to the idle wake path when the full path does not apply.
Tickless balancing cross-call clears pending kick state, signals a programming error when the expected kick indication was absent, and requests scheduler soft processing only when the target is idle.
Tickless scheduler flags for a processor reside as a field inside that processor run queue object.

Permission to stop the periodic tick denies deadline work, multiple round robin members, bandwidth constrained lone fair work and negative extended scheduler advice, while allowing a lone round robin, FIFO only, or unconstrained lone fair and extended configurations.
Bandwidth sensitivity for tick permission applies narrowly to a lone queued fair current task.

Extended scheduler tick permission allows stopping when the current entity is outside that class or none of that class is accounted, denies during bypass or while the current entity is under rescue, and otherwise follows a per-queue stop indicator; a minimal build always allows stopping.
Inspection of the rescue occupant of a run queue requires holding that queue lock; builds without subordinate scheduler support report no occupant.

Bandwidth constrained reporting for a fair task is affirmative only when global bandwidth control is in use and either local runtime control or hierarchical quota restriction applies; other builds always report unconstrained.
Ownership mapping from a task to its fair run queue resolves either through the scheduling entity linkage or through the task processor queue, depending on build configuration.
Hierarchy walk over task groups offers paired downward and upward visitation with early termination on visitor error and completion upon return to the starting group.
Provides a no-op group visitor that unconditionally reports success and ignores its context argument.

Scheduling weight derivation uses a dedicated idle magnitude for idle policy tasks and a priority indexed table otherwise, optionally propagating changes through the owning class reweight hook when load update is requested.
Idle policy classification recognizes exactly the designated idle scheduling policy value.
System wide utilization clamp controls for minimum, maximum and real time minimum default to the full capacity scale value.
Refresh of the real time minimum request for a task requires holding its priority inheritance lock and preserves any value explicitly set by the user.
Default minimum synchronization applies only to real time tasks and serializes against queueing and migration by holding the task queue lock during the update.
Exposes the effective clamp magnitude for a task, using the annotated active value when the task is currently accounted and otherwise computing the effective result.

Re-accounting of a task clamp on its queue applies only to active entries, refreshes queue aggregates by paired removal and addition, and clears the queue idle marker when maximum clamp activity resumes.

Activation refresh for all clamp indexes of a task holds the task queue lock, covering even queues previously associated with non-runnable tasks to order updates against enqueue, dequeue and migration.
Task queue locking acquires the run queue together with the task priority inheritance lock and releases both while restoring interrupt state.
Provides iteration over all tasks attached to a control group state in order to refresh their active clamp accounting.
Root group clamp refresh propagates system minimum and maximum controls into the root request state and recomputes effective hierarchy state; an alternate build performs no action.
Effective hierarchy recomputation requires holding the clamp mutex while under read side control group protection.
Hierarchy recomputation signals a usage error when invoked without required read side protection.

Effective clamp derivation caps each group request by its parent effective value and caps protection by limit, updates only changed buckets, prunes unchanged subtrees, and refreshes runnable members upon change.
Mapping from a control group scheduler state pointer to its enclosing task group follows the containing structure and yields null for null input.

Synchronization of the real time minimum default combines task list ordering barriers with iteration over all threads so that concurrent thread creation observes either the new task or the new default.

Control handler for clamp system controls validates ordering and capacity bounds, restores prior values on parsing or validation failure, enables clamp accounting on effective change, and propagates minimum, maximum and real time defaults to their respective destinations.
Global clamp hierarchy mutations are serialized by a dedicated mutex object.
Clamp usage tracking starts disabled and transitions to enabled upon first activation, while an alternate build provides an empty enable operation.

Fork handling clears active clamp markers and optionally resets requests when reset on fork is set, post-fork handling synchronizes the real time default, and early initialization marks queues idle with unrestricted defaults; alternate builds are no-ops.
Reports whether a task is currently present in queued state on its run queue.

Sampling of a blocked task wait address requires holding its priority inheritance lock with interrupts disabled, excludes the caller and running, waking or queued tasks, and orders against concurrent wakeup.
Deactivation marks a task as migrating before removal from its queue, with that marker remaining set until a later enqueue clears it.
Deactivation signals a usage error when invoked with the sleep dequeue flag.
Reports whether a given task is the current occupant of its processor.
Testing of a task state mask serializes against real time lock waiting and freezer transitions by holding the priority inheritance lock with interrupts disabled.
